content.title: European High-Speed Trains
content.text: Want to get there really fast? How does up to 300 kilometres per hour sound? Europe has a wide network of high-speed trains that take you quickly to your destination. High-speed train services only stop at major cities. The trains offer comfortable 1st and 2nd class cars and good catering services. Many European high-speed trains are included in the Interrail Pass, but the reservations for these trains are not included in your Pass. Reservations for high-speed trains are often mandatory and need to be booked in advance. Your reservation will guarantee you a seat. You can book your seat for most high-speeds trains up to 3 months in advance. Don't forget your seat reservations! Some trains in Europe require a seat reservation, most commonly in France, Italy, and Spain. Reservation fees are charged by the railway carriers, and are not included in your Interrail Pass. Read all about reservations → Alfa Pendular (Portugal) Find out about Portugal's Alfa Pendular high-speed train, travelling on the route Braga - Porto - Coimbra - Lisbon - Faro. Experience comfort and convenience on your Interrail trip through Portugal. Alvia (Spain) The Spanish Alvia trains combine both a long distance and a high-speed service to connect major cities across Spain. Find out more. Avant (Spain) The Avant is a high-speed long-distance train that connects the Spanish capital Madrid to the southern cities. Find out more. AVE (Spain) The AVE is a modern high-speed train in Spain that connects many cities across the country. Find out more. Eurocity Direct and Eurocity Eurocity Direct and Eurocity are new reservation-free high-speed trains connecting major cities in Belgium and the Netherlands. Find out more. Euromed (Spain) The Euromed high-speed train travels along the Mediterranean coast from Barcelona to Alicante. Find out more. Eurostar (Great Britain, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany) The high-speed Eurostar is the best option for a trip to London from Brussels or Paris, and then onwards to Amsterdam or Cologne. Travel is covered with your Interrail Pass! Express InterCity Premium Express InterCity Premium is the fastest train on the Polish network connecting many major cities of Poland. Find out more. ICE (Germany, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, France, Switzerland, Netherlands) The ICE (InterCity Express) is a high-speed train that connects all major cities in Germany. Find out more. Iryo (Spain) Iryo high-speed trains connect Madrid to other major cities in Spain, from Barcelona and Valencia to Seville, Cuenca and more. Travel in comfort across Spain with your Interrail Pass. Le Frecce (Italy) The Le Frecce are a series of modern high-speed trains connecting cities and towns all across Italy. Find out more. SJ (Sweden) SJ high-speed trains travel from Stockholm to other cities in Sweden, as well as to Copenhagen in Denmark. Find out more! SNCF TGV INOUI and RENFE AVE (Spain, France) SNCF TGV INOUI and RENFE AVE are international high-speed trains connecting Spain and France. Find out more. SuperCity (Czech Republic) The SuperCity high-speed train is the newest and fastest addition to the Czech Railways fleet. Read more! TGV (France) The TGV is a high-speed train that operates all over France and beyond. Find out more. TGV Lyria (France, Switzerland) The TGV Lyria is an international high-speed train that connects France and Switzerland. Find out more. Train reservations for high-speed trains Reservations are mandatory for some high-speed trains. Depending on the train, you can make these reservations online, by phone or at the train station. A reservation guarantees you a seat on the train, which is quite useful if you are travelling with a group and want to sit together. Read more about reservations If you have a need for speed, or want to travel at night to save costs, we've got you covered. Find out more about the many other train types in Europe.
